literal: In the fourth year he was made Chief Rectifier of the Imperial Clan and advanced to duke.
idiomatic: Year 4 he became Chief Rectifier and was advanced to duke.

literal: When the great army campaigned east, Yi with Junior Mentor Yang Yi held Zhiguan Pass and at once was made Inspector of Huai.
idiomatic: On the eastern campaign Yi with Yang Yi held Zhiguan and was made Huai Inspector.

literal: At the beginning of Tianhe he followed Duke of Shangyong Lu Teng in attacking the rebellious Man of Xinzhou, Ran Lingxian and others.
idiomatic: At Tianhe's start he followed Duke Lu Teng of Shangyong against Xinzhou rebels Ran Lingxian and others.

literal: Yi entered by the Kaizhou route, first sent envoys to proclaim fortune and calamity, and the tribes all submitted.
idiomatic: He entered by Kaizhou, proclaimed fortune and ruin, and the tribes submitted.

literal: He held the posts of Inspector of Xin and Tong in succession.
idiomatic: He governed Xin and Tong in turn.

literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as Grand General and made Inspector of Xining, but before reaching his post he died in the capital.
idiomatic: Year 6 he was summoned Grand General and Xining Inspector but died in the capital before taking post.

literal: Yi was frugal by nature and did not pursue production; the salary he received he gave entirely to kin;
idiomatic: Yi lived plainly and gave all salary to kin;

literal: at the day of his death the house had no surplus wealth.
idiomatic: at his death the house held nothing.

literal: His dwelling was low and shabby; there was no place for the mourning hall—an edict built a shrine for him.
idiomatic: His house was mean; no hall for mourning—an edict raised a shrine.

literal: Posthumously his former office, with addition of Inspector of Si, posthumous name Ding.
idiomatic: Posthumously his rank plus Si Inspector, posthumous name Ding.

literal: Son Kan inherited.
idiomatic: Son Kan inherited.

literal: Kan, styled Daoyuan, was resolute and brave from youth; before the capping age he already followed the army.
idiomatic: Kan, styled Daoyuan, was bold young and took the field before capping age.

literal: He held the post of Administrator of Lean, and for military merit was added Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Marshal with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: He governed Lean, and for merit gained Agile Cavalry Grand General and Grand Marshal equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: Transferred to Inspector of Yan, he did not reach his post and died.
idiomatic: Shifted to Yan Inspector, he died before arriving.

literal: Posthumously his former office, with addition of Inspector of Yu, posthumous name Hui.
idiomatic: Posthumously his rank plus Yu Inspector, posthumous name Hui.

literal: Son Yun inherited.
idiomatic: Son Yun inherited.

literal: Chuzhi's younger brother Yue, styled Baolong, married the Princess of Zhao Commandery and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.
idiomatic: Younger brother Yue, styled Baolong, wed Princess of Zhao and became Commandant of Horse Guards.

literal: He replaced his elder brother as commander of the Yunzhong garrison, was made Inspector of Shuo, acting General Who Pacifies the North, and Duke of Henei.
idiomatic: He replaced his brother at Yunzhong, became Shuo Inspector, acting General Who Pacifies the North, Duke of Henei.

literal: He memorialized asking to abolish the Hexi park preserve and grant the land to people for cultivation.
idiomatic: He asked to open the Hexi imperial park to settlers.

literal: The offices held fast and reported: this park is where elk gather and the Imperial Kitchen draws supply; if granted to people, they feared something would be lacking.
idiomatic: Offices objected: elk feed the kitchen; opening it might leave a shortfall.

literal: Yue pressed the request firmly; Emperor Xiaowen followed it.
idiomatic: Yue pressed on; Xiaowen agreed.

literal: Returned as Minister of the Imperial Clan, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and tutor to Prince of Yingchuan, and died.
idiomatic: He returned as Minister of the Imperial Clan, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, tutor to Prince of Yingchuan, then died.

literal: Father and son Chuzhi in succession garrisoned Yunzhong; the northern soil submitted to their might and virtue.
idiomatic: Father and son held Yunzhong in turn; the north honored their might and virtue.

literal: Among the Sima clan who returned north in the time of Huan Xuan and Liu Yu were also Sima Jingzhi, Shufan, and Tianzhu, all holding lofty posts.
idiomatic: Other Simas who fled north in the days of Huan Xuan and Liu Yu—Jingzhi, Shufan, Tianzhu—also rose high.

literal: Jingzhi, styled Honglue, was a descendant of Jin Prince of Runan Liang.
idiomatic: Jingzhi, styled Honglue, descended from Jin's Prince Liang of Runan.

literal: In the Mingyuan era he came to court, was enfeoffed Duke of Cangwu, and added Grand General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: In Mingyuan he came to court, was made Duke of Cangwu and Grand General Who Pacifies the South.

literal: He was upright and had integrity.
idiomatic: He was upright and principled.

literal: He died; posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Runan.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Prince of Runan.

literal: Son Shizi inherited the title.
idiomatic: Son Shizi inherited.

literal: Jingzhi's elder brother Zhun, styled Juzhi, returned to Wei at the end of Taichang.
idiomatic: Elder brother Zhun, styled Juzhi, came to Wei late in Taichang.

literal: Enfeoffed Duke of Xin'an.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Duke of Xin'an.

literal: Made Administrator of Guangning, changed to Marquis of Miling.
idiomatic: He governed Guangning, then was made Marquis of Miling.

literal: He died; son Anguo inherited the title.
idiomatic: He died; son Anguo inherited.

literal: Shufan was a descendant of Jin Prince of Anping, Duke Xian Fu.
idiomatic: Shufan descended from Jin's Prince Xian Fu of Anping.

literal: His father Tanzhi was Jin Prince of Hejian.
idiomatic: His father Tanzhi was Jin Prince of Hejian.

literal: In the time of Huan Xuan and Liu Yu, Shufan with his elder brother Guo Fan fled to Murong Chao.
idiomatic: In the turmoil Shufan and brother Guo Fan fled to Murong Chao.

literal: Later he went to Yao Hong.
idiomatic: Later he joined Yao Hong.

literal: When Hong was destroyed, he fled to Qu Mugai.
idiomatic: When Hong fell he fled to Qu Mugai.

literal: When Tongwan was pacified, the brothers both entered Wei.
idiomatic: When Tongwan fell both brothers entered Wei.

literal: Guo Fan was enfeoffed Duke of Huainan; Shufan was enfeoffed Marquis of Danyang.
idiomatic: Guo Fan became Duke of Huainan; Shufan Marquis of Danyang.

literal: Tianzhu was himself son of Jin General of Agile Cavalry Yuanxian.
idiomatic: Tianzhu was son of Jin's Agile Cavalry General Yuanxian.

literal: Coming to court, he was enfeoffed Duke of Donghai and held the posts of Inspector of Qing and Yan in succession.
idiomatic: At court he was Duke of Donghai and dual Inspector of Qing and Yan.

literal: Chang loved dogs and horses and delighted in military affairs.
idiomatic: Chang loved hounds and horses and delighted in arms.

literal: Having entered Wei and passed through several reigns, he still wore plain cloth and black cap, the same garb as for fierce mourning.
idiomatic: In Wei through several reigns he still wore plain cloth and black cap like mourning dress.

literal: Yet he would shout at and beat servants; his speech mixed barbarian and Chinese.
idiomatic: Yet he abused servants in a mixed barbarian-Chinese tongue.

literal: Even in public sessions the princes would each mock and toy with him.
idiomatic: Even in open court the princes mocked him.

literal: Some would twist his hand and bite his arm until he was wounded in pain; the sound of their laughter reached the emperor's hearing.
idiomatic: Some twisted his hand or bit his arm till he cried; laughter reached the throne.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen always treated him with extra favor and did not regard it as strange to question.
idiomatic: Xiaowen always indulged him and never took offense.

literal: But when he memorialized on affairs of his native state and spoke of levies and corvée, he would compose his face and weep; grief moved those beside him.
idiomatic: Yet memorializing on his old country and corvée he wept till all beside him grieved.

literal: Yet by nature he was narrow and quick; joy and anger were not constant.
idiomatic: By nature he was narrow and volatile.

literal: Whenever wrath flared, the cudgel and switch were especially harsh;
idiomatic: In rage his beatings were savage;

literal: toward southern gentlemen his courtesy was often lacking.
idiomatic: toward southerners his courtesy often failed.

literal: Because of this, men harbored fear and kept away.
idiomatic: Men feared him and kept their distance.

literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was transferred to Director of the Inner Court's Grand Provisioners.
idiomatic: Early in Taihe he became Director of the Inner Court's Grand Provisioners.

literal: At the beginning of Qi an edict had Chang and the generals campaign south.
idiomatic: At Qi's founding Chang was ordered south with the generals.

literal: Passing Xuzhou, he wept and bowed at his mother's old hall; grief moved those who followed.
idiomatic: At Xuzhou he wept at his mother's old hall and moved his escort.

literal: He then went everywhere through his old dwellings; at each place tears fell, and those beside him could not keep from stinging in the nose.
idiomatic: He walked his old streets weeping; companions wept with him.

literal: When he reached the army's place and was about to take the field, he bowed on four sides to the officers and soldiers and himself declared that his house and state were destroyed and he was covered by the court's kindness.
idiomatic: Before battle he bowed to the ranks, saying his state was gone and only the court's grace remained.

literal: His words were cutting and true, his voice excited and rising; tears streamed; the whole army was moved to sigh.
idiomatic: His words were keen, his voice fierce; tears ran; the whole army sighed.

literal: Later Chang, fearing that rain would soon come, memorialized asking to withdraw the army, and it was granted.
idiomatic: Later, fearing rain, he asked to withdraw and was allowed.

literal: Again added Grand Marshal with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies and head of the Ministry of Rites.
idiomatic: He was again Grand Marshal equal to the Three Excellencies and head of Rites.

literal: At the time the court was reforming court ceremony; an edict had Chang and Jiang Shaoyou take sole charge of the matter.
idiomatic: The court reformed ritual; Chang and Jiang Shaoyou were put in sole charge.

literal: Chang listed the old forms upward; scarcely anything was forgotten.
idiomatic: Chang listed the old forms and forgot almost nothing.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen at the Xuanwen Hall summoned Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishi to enter the feast and told Chang: "Jishi is a frontier chieftain—not enough to match the rites due feudal lords.
idiomatic: At Xuanwen Hall Xiaowen feasted Prince Yang Jishi of Wuxing and told Chang, "A frontier chief cannot match feudal rites—yet the throne does not disdain small states' ministers, so we trouble you nobles here.

literal: Yet the king does not disdain the minister of a small state, and therefore has wearied you, duke and ministers, here.
idiomatic: That is why you are wearied here.

literal: Again made Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He was again Director of the Secretariat.

literal: When the five ranks were established, Chang was enfeoffed Duke of Qi Commandery with the added title of King of Song.
idiomatic: When five ranks were founded he was Duke of Qi Commandery with the added title King of Song.

literal: In the seventeenth year Xiaowen at the Jingwu Hall held great discussion of the southern campaign.
idiomatic: Year 17 Xiaowen at Jingwu Hall debated the southern war.

literal: When talk touched the usurpations of Liu and Xiao, Chang would weep without end.
idiomatic: Speaking of Liu and Xiao usurpations he wept without cease.

literal: The emperor also wept for it; his courtesy toward Chang grew ever more exalted.
idiomatic: The emperor wept too and honored him the more.

literal: In the eighteenth year he was made Commissioner with credentials, Area Commander of Wu, Yue, Chu, and Pengcheng forces, Grand General, and Grand Marshal, garrisoning Xuzhou.
idiomatic: Year 18 he was Commissioner, area commander of Wu, Yue, Chu, and Pengcheng, Grand General and Grand Marshal at Xuzhou.

literal: Chang repeatedly memorialized declining the post of Grand General; the edict did not permit it.
idiomatic: He repeatedly declined Grand General; the throne refused.

literal: At his departure the emperor personally saw him off and ordered the hundred officials to compose poems to present to Chang.
idiomatic: At departure the emperor feasted him and ordered poems from the hundred offices.

literal: He also gave him one collection of his own writings.
idiomatic: He also gave a volume of his own writings.

literal: The emperor then showed him the brushwork he himself had composed and said: "The times fit ending slaughter; affairs turn on literary enterprise.
idiomatic: The emperor showed his own writing and said, "Times favor ending slaughter; affairs turn on letters.

literal: Though I do not study, I cannot bear to stop.
idiomatic: Though I do not study, I cannot stop.

literal: On a whim I wished you to see them, and therefore show them—though they have no flavor worth speaking of, they may still raise a laugh.
idiomatic: I wished you to see them—thin fare, but perhaps a laugh.

literal: He valued Chang to this degree.
idiomatic: He valued Chang to that degree.

literal: From the time Chang left Pengcheng until now was long; his former fasting halls, mountains, and pools still stood;
idiomatic: Long since he left Pengcheng his old halls, hills, and pools still stood;

literal: Chang repaired them anew and dwelt within them again.
idiomatic: Chang restored them and lived there again.

literal: He could not soothe the frontier and cherish men, comfort and receive old associates, yet within the inner gates it was noisy and vulgar, inside and outside mixed with villainy, and old officials all sighed in regret.
idiomatic: He failed the border and old friends while his household grew riotous and corrupt; veterans sighed.

literal: He prepared his tomb southwest of Pengcheng, in the same mound as the Third Princess but in a separate chamber.
idiomatic: He prepared a tomb southwest of Pengcheng, sharing a mound with the Third Princess but not her vault.

literal: When stone was piled the mound collapsed and crushed more than ten men to death.
idiomatic: While piling stone the mound collapsed and killed more than ten.

literal: Later it was moved and altered again; public and private expense was harmed.
idiomatic: Later it was moved again at great public and private cost.

literal: Chang's eldest son Chengxu was born of the princess, his principal wife.
idiomatic: Eldest son Chengxu was the princess's child.

literal: Sickly from youth, he married Emperor Xiaowen's sister Princess of Pengcheng, was Commandant of Horse Guards, and died before Chang.
idiomatic: Frail from youth, he wed Xiaowen's sister Princess of Pengcheng, was Commandant of Horse Guards, and predeceased Chang.

literal: Chengxu's son Hui, styled Chongchang, was heir and inherited the fief.
idiomatic: Chengxu's son Hui, styled Chongchang, was heir and inherited.

literal: He married Emperor Xuanwu's second elder sister Princess of Lanling.
idiomatic: He married Xuanwu's second elder sister, Princess of Lanling.

literal: The princess was fiercely jealous; Hui once secretly favored her waiting maid.
idiomatic: The princess was fiercely jealous; Hui once lay with her maid.

literal: She became pregnant; the princess flogged her to death;
idiomatic: The maid conceived; the princess beat her dead;

literal: cut open the pregnancy, dismembered it limb by limb, stuffed the maid's belly with straw, and displayed her naked to Hui.
idiomatic: she cut out the child, dismembered it, stuffed straw in the maid's belly, and showed the corpse naked to Hui.

literal: Hui then nursed resentment and grew cold toward the princess.
idiomatic: Hui nursed hatred and grew cold toward her.

literal: The princess's elder sister, entering to hear lectures, told Empress Dowager Ling the cause.
idiomatic: Her elder sister, attending lectures at court, told Empress Dowager Ling.

literal: The empress dowager ordered Prince of Qinghe Yi to investigate the affair to the end.
idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered Prince Yi of Qinghe to investigate.

literal: Yi with Prince of Gaoyang Yong and Prince of Guangping Huai memorialized their disharmony and asked divorce and removal of enfeoffment.
idiomatic: Yi with Prince Yong of Gaoyang and Prince Huai of Guangping reported their strife and sought divorce and loss of rank.

literal: The empress dowager followed it.
idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed.

literal: The princess was in the palace a full year; Yong and the others repeatedly asked permission to restore the old bond.
idiomatic: A year in the palace Yong and others repeatedly asked to restore the marriage.

literal: The empress dowager wept as she sent the princess back and admonished her to be cautious and restrained.
idiomatic: The empress dowager wept sending her back and warned her to be restrained.

literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang Hui again secretly debauched the daughters of the Zhang and Chen families.
idiomatic: Early in Zhengguang Hui again lay secretly with daughters of Zhang and Chen.

literal: The princess no longer checked or forbade it.
idiomatic: The princess no longer restrained him.
